identity.description: Autoregressive integrated moving-average forecaster for a single time-indexed series; models autocorrelation and (with seasonal terms) periodicity, producing horizon forecasts with prediction intervals.

consumes.note: targetSpec `series` — a value indexed by a regular time step, NOT a row-matrix; the regime that proves the template beyond tabular

emits.note: point forecast + prediction intervals over the horizon

invariances.why: a linear time-series model is equivariant to rescaling the series; forecasts rescale with it
a log transform changes additive vs multiplicative seasonality — it is a modeling choice, not a no-op
the likelihood needs a regular, gap-free series; missing periods must be interpolated or the frequency re-set
operates on a single numeric series; exogenous categoricals only via SARIMAX design columns
assumes (weak) STATIONARITY after differencing and roughly Gaussian innovations for valid intervals
seasonal orders need multiple full cycles of history; short series flag a fall-back to a naive/ETS floor
the whole purpose is forecasting beyond observed time — with widening intervals

featureStats.why: lag-k autocorrelation reveals periodicity the seasonal orders must capture; near-zero flags plain ARIMA over SARIMA
a strong trend signals the differencing order d and warns against a stationary-only fit
too few seasonal cycles means the seasonal orders are unidentifiable — a gate to a simpler floor

modelMetrics.why: MASE against the seasonal-naive floor is the honest forecast scoreboard; MASE>=1 means the model does not beat repeating last season

driver.wrapperNeeds: series adapter: (time_col, value_col, freq, horizon); predict becomes forecast(horizon) not per-row predict

placementClaims.why: gaps must be filled to a regular series before fitting; but time-aware interpolation, not tabular median
a log transform converts multiplicative seasonality to additive, often improving the fit
scale-equivariant; standardization changes nothing about the fit
single numeric series has nothing to encode (exogenous regressors are a SARIMAX concern, not preprocessing)
